answer.rationale: With the contract expiring in 14 days and the line running at 94% of committed volume with zero buffer, any option requiring migration or onboarding (switch_primary_vendor, add_second_source) risks a delivery interruption Halden cannot absorb right now. memory_c1 and memory_c6 indicate the incumbent relationship is stable and has supported volume-based cost reductions before, while memory_c4 shows that benchmarking-driven renegotiation at renewal previously recovered real margin on both price and terms without any migration work. Given the finance mandate for an 18% spend cut, negotiate_terms lets us pursue meaningful cost reduction within the 14-day window while preserving continuity of supply. I verified memory_c4 specifically because it is the load-bearing precedent for this action, and confirming its original context (scope of savings, whether incumbent leverage was unusual) materially changes confidence in expecting similar recovery now. I flag downstream risk because a hard negotiating stance close to contract expiry could still provoke incumbent pushback or delay, so this is not a value-neutral choice, and the switch/second-source options remain unresolved for next cycle. I'm not certain the same margin recovery is achievable this time given tighter timing and mandated cost pressure, so this should be treated as a bounded, monitored move rather than a settled outcome.
